title: Gap Amplification for Local Hamiltonians with Combinatorial Soundness
authors: Mitali Bafna, Quynh T. Nguyen, Tina Zhang
abstract: The quantum PCP conjecture is one of the major open problems in quantum complexity theory. It has resisted attack in part because many primitives used in the proof of the classical PCP theorem, such as locality-preserving gap amplification and alphabet reduction, have no obvious quantum analogues due to quantum no-cloning. Locality-preserving gap amplification is a procedure that takes as input a local Hamiltonian problem instance and produces a new instance with a larger promise gap, without increasing the locality of the Hamiltonian, and instead moderately increasing its local qudit dimension. Obtaining this kind of control over the locality during gap amplification is critical to the success of many known strategies for proving the classical PCP theorem. In this work, we put forth the first known viable template for quantum locality-preserving gap amplification, and we prove that our procedure amplifies the combinatorial gap of local Hamiltonians. Our work introduces a new framework for reasoning about quantum gap amplification in terms of fault-tolerant computation, and illuminates a route toward importing one of the central ingredients in classical PCPs into the quantum setting. In particular, we build upon ideas from the recent classical PCP of Bafna--Minzer--Vyas based on high-dimensional expanders, and the circuit-to-Hamiltonian construction of Anshu--Breuckmann--Nguyen, in addition to several recent advances in quantum coding theory.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, viable template for quantum locality-preserving gap amplification, a critical missing piece for proving the quantum PCP conjecture. By showing how to amplify the gap of local Hamiltonians while controlling locality, the authors provide a major theoretical advance in quantum complexity theory. This work bridges classical PCP techniques into the quantum domain using advanced concepts from quantum coding and fault-tolerant computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of translating the classical PCP theorem into the quantum setting, specifically by developing a method for locality-preserving gap amplification.
main_result: The authors present the first viable template for quantum locality-preserving gap amplification, proving that this procedure successfully amplifies the combinatorial gap of local Hamiltonians.
method: The technique combines ideas from classical PCP proofs using high-dimensional expanders and circuit-to-Hamiltonian constructions, focusing on distributing fault-tolerant 'violation information' rather than repeating the witness.
model_or_system: The work is framed around local Hamiltonian problems, which are used to model quantum constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) and are central to the quantum PCP conjecture.
key_observables: Combinatorial energy ($\epsilon$), ground energy, and the gap of the local Hamiltonian.
important_parameters: The gap regime (low-gap vs. high-gap) dictates the polynomial scaling of the required qudit dimension and log-alphabet size.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on developing novel techniques for fault-tolerant computation and assumes the existence of asymptotically good quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs) for certain bounds.
paper_structure: The paper builds conceptually by first establishing the necessity of locality-preserving gap amplification for the quantum PCP conjecture, then presenting the template using existing tools (HDX, circuit-to-Hamiltonian), and finally detailing the resulting combinatorial soundness proof.
why_interesting: The development of locality-preserving gap amplification is a crucial theoretical tool for quantum complexity theory, providing a pathway to tackle the quantum PCP conjecture by importing a key classical ingredient.
